result.topic_en: Euler gives the velocity formula for water flowing out through a short narrow tube CD. He notes that a very small opening can stop the outflow entirely, and specializes the formulas to the case of a fully open tube (𝔥 = 1), concluding that the motion becomes uniform whenever 𝔤 < 1.

99. Notandum autem eſt, quantumuis altitudo tubuli $CD=c$ fuerit exigua, tamen eam ob rationes ante expoſitas maiorem capi debere, et quo minor fuerit eius amplitudo $bb$, eo magis altitudo vera $c$ augeri debebit. Etiamſi ergo tubulus $CD$ fuerit breviſſimus, ſeu quaſi foraminulum per laminam pertuſum, fractio $\frac{\alpha c}{b}$ eo maiorem habebit valorem, quo minus fuerit foraminulum, ſeu quo minus fuerit $b$. Cum igitur hoc caſu $e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{b}}$ fiat numerus valde paruus, perſpicuum eſt, foraminulum tam paruum fieri poſſe, vt aqua per id plane non effluat.

100. Si tubulus $DC$ in $DD$ penitus ſit apertus, erit $\mathfrak{h}=1$ et caſu priori habebitur:
$v=\frac{e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}(a+l-\frac{1}{\alpha}g\cos.\zeta)+\frac{1}{\alpha}(g\cos.\zeta+b)-e^{\frac{\alpha c}{b}}(l+\frac{1}{\alpha}b)}{1+(e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}-1)\mathfrak{g}}$
Pro caſu autem poſteriori habebitur:
$v=\frac{e^{\frac{-\alpha b\cos.\zeta-\alpha b\sin.\zeta}{g}}(a+l-\frac{1}{\alpha}g)+\frac{1}{\alpha}e^{\frac{-\alpha b\sin.\zeta}{g}}g+\frac{1}{\alpha}b-e^{\frac{\alpha c}{b}}(l+\frac{1}{\alpha}b)}{1+(e^{\frac{-\alpha b\cos.\zeta-\alpha b\sin.\zeta}{g}}-1)\mathfrak{g}}$
quoties ergo eſt $\mathfrak{g}<1$, aquae motus ſemper ad ſtatum vniformitatis pertinget.

items.english: Therefore, even if the tube CD is very short, or like a small hole bored through a plate, the fraction αc/b will have a larger value the smaller the hole is, that is, the smaller b is.

items.quote: Cum igitur hoc caſu $e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{b}}$ fiat numerus valde paruus, perſpicuum eſt, foraminulum tam paruum fieri poſſe, vt aqua per id plane non effluat.
items.english: Since in this case e^{-αc/b} becomes a very small number, it is evident that a hole can be made so small that water does not flow through it at all.

items.quote: quoties ergo eſt $\mathfrak{g}<1$, aquae motus ſemper ad ſtatum vniformitatis pertinget.
items.english: Therefore, whenever 𝔤 < 1, the motion of the water will always reach a state of uniformity.
